replacements.text: Strongest feature: Flew separates logical necessity from experiential regularity, observing that known causes concern intracosmic events and thereby challenging Craig’s extrapolation to the universe’s beginning. Principal limitation: This distinction defeats deductive certainty but does not show that beginning to exist becomes explanatorily irrelevant at the cosmic boundary; moreover, “arbitrary” understates Craig’s independent metaphysical intuition. Live burden: Flew must identify which constitutive feature of intracosmic causation disappears in cosmic origination, while Craig must justify a non-temporal causal relation without depending on spacetime-bound experience. Locked score: The exact 81 reflects logical coherence 81, evidence warrant 72, responsiveness 89, relevance and burden 85, precision and clarity 83, and calibration and charity 74: a sharply targeted, intelligible reply whose evidential incompleteness and overstatement restrain its otherwise substantial force.

Strongest feature: Flew isolates the disanalogy: a little bang occurs intracosmically, whereas the Big Bang originates the universe itself, so causal expectations cannot automatically transfer. Principal limitation: Domain difference blocks comparison but does not prove their shared characteristic of beginning causally irrelevant, leaving Craig’s metaphysical principle available unless Flew identifies the decisive difference. Live burden: Flew must specify which spacetime-dependent conditions make causation applicable to small events yet inapplicable to cosmic origination, while Craig must defend trans-spatiotemporal causation independently of the analogy. Locked score: The exact 82 reflects logical coherence 82, evidence warrant 70, responsiveness 90, relevance and burden 84, precision and clarity 89, and calibration and charity 80: exceptionally direct, precise engagement whose modest evidential foundation cannot exclude a broader causal principle.
